description: Any eligible US stock. Second-order effects: events traced to a company the news never names.

trades.thesis: TJX beat and raised on 11-18 (comps +4% vs plan 2-3%, FY comp now 4%, Marmaxx improved) and Target posted +5.6% comps on +5% traffic. US control retail sales came in at +0.6% vs 0.4%. Ross reports Q3 on 11-19 after the close with 8 straight EPS beats and comps of +7% and +10% in the last two quarters. It fell 4 days into the print and has lagged TJX's rebound. The edge is Ross's own print, since the sympathy gap is already in the fill price.

causal_chain.step: TJX Q3 FY27 (11-18 BMO): comps +4% vs 2-3% plan and 3.8% consensus, FY comp raised to 4%, Marmaxx improved. Target comps +5.6% on +5.0% traffic. Both show strong off-price and value traffic in the Aug-Oct quarter.

Ross competes for the same shopper as Marmaxx, and its quarter ended around Oct 31. Core retail sales beat (+0.6% vs 0.4%), so the same demand should show in Ross's Q3 comps. Ross has beaten EPS 8 of 8 quarters, with consensus EPS about $1.85 on $6.2B revenue.

ROST reports 11-19 after the close, and the reaction lands in my 3-day horizon. Weakest link: TJX's Marmaxx comp was only +2%, so strength may not transfer to Ross. The sympathy gap at today's open is already in my fill price.

sessions.feedback: No blocking issues. Two small requests. (1) Pre-market prices for scan/get_quotes come with a lag, and the open auction price is unknown, so for names that gap on overnight news (SPY -1.5% since the close) I am sizing off stale numbers. (2) An earnings calendar for the coming week, with BMO/AMC and consensus, would save several web searches. The scan 'earnings' field only covers the last two sessions and the next five, and sometimes shows 'time not given'. Also, scan labels SHOE's earnings as 'none' although it reported this morning, so that field misses same-day reports for some tickers.

The research budget ran out before I could write my notes file, so tomorrow's session starts from this summary and the old notes. A small allowance for a notes update after the budget message would help. read_page failed on Yahoo Finance article URLs again. ETFs such as SPY and QQQ don't appear to be tradable, so I can't express a clean market-beta view. A tool that returned a live intraday market snapshot would help on volatile gap days.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two small things: read_page on prnewswire returned only navigation and no release body, so I had to rely on web_search snippets from the code tool. It would also help to know whether a stop that gaps through at the open fills at the open price or at the stop price. That decides whether closing manually into a gap beats letting the stop work.

Nothing blocked me, but two things would help.
1. The digest and news feed lag same-morning earnings. WSM, BABA and WMT prints were only in the news feed or web search, and I had to use web_search to find the WSM numbers. An earnings-results feed with EPS/revenue vs consensus and guidance for companies that reported pre-market would save calls.
2. scan shows pre-market only as a percent and a share count. An indication of whether the pre-market print is from IEX only or all venues would help me judge thin prints.

No blocking problems this session. Two things would have saved time. First, an earnings-consensus field (EPS and revenue expectations, and the typical post-earnings move) in scan, because I had to run web searches for it. Second, a sympathy-gap estimate: pre-market prints under 1,000 shares are too thin to judge the fill price for a read-through trade, and orders fill at the open, so I can't tell how much of the move I'll pay for. web_search is only reachable from inside code_execution and returns a JSON string, which costs extra calls. read_page on Benzinga still fails.

Digest 'biggest pre-market movers' ranks thin prints (100-600 shares) by sd, so most of the list is noise (e.g., KNX -8.5% on 396 shares). Filtering on minimum shares or a percent-of-average-day threshold would save budget. A tool returning the biggest losers and gainers of the previous session (not only gainers) would help find overreactions. A 'peers with earnings dates in the next 5 days' lookup by industry would suit the lagging-peer strategy.

Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

- SHOE (-22%): small cap, 0.5% slippage.
- ADI (-13% on a beat), BURL (+8% on a miss), SNY, OTLY: no edge.

Notes updated: general notes plus HPE, ANT and CRWV ticker notes.

- Tooling: web_search only works via code_execution and returns a JSON STRING (json.loads it; IMPORT json IN EVERY CELL). Earnings-day shortcut: news() on tickers gives the press-release numbers at ~12:30 UTC; web_search for 'consensus' gives beat/miss vs street.
- Macro regime (Nov 2026): 10y ~5.1%, PPI 6.5% y/y, hot CPI 3 months, Fed hike in Dec priced ~100% (Williams 11-23: more hikes possible, 'work to do'), Warsh Fed chair. Iran/Hormuz: Brent ~$90 (-22% in 4 weeks, lowest since Aug). AI-bust phase: SMH -35% from June high, NVDA -32% from high even after +31.5% on 11-23, neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS, IREN, APLD) -65% to -79% from highs, VRT/ORCL/DELL -44 to -55%. Cause chain: Huang resigned 11-12 (national-security/personal reports), SEC exam of NVDA accounting, California AG subpoena, H200 China halt, rule on remote access by foreign data centers. 11-23: Huang reinstated (Trump administration pushed) -> NVDA +31.5%, QQQ +7.0%, SPY +4.71% (best day since Apr 2025), SPY close 722.29. 11-24 pre-market: SPY -1.5%, QQQ -2.4%, NVDA -6%, AI names -5%. Core PCE/GDP 11-25 8:30 ET (consensus core PCE 0.3% m/m, 3.2% y/y); Thanksgiving 11-26.
- BOUNCE-FADE PATTERN: AI names opened at the high on 11-23 (NBIS open 110.00 = high, close 97.80, close-in-range 0.14; CRWV, APLD, IREN, SNDK, TSM, SPCX closed in the bottom 15% of the range). Earlier fades: NBIS 11-11 +15% then 11-12 -17%; 11-19 pre-market bounce reversed. Beat-and-raise gets sold in this tape: HPE rev +50%, FY27 EPS guide 5.05-5.35 vs 4.74, -12% pre-market (AI margin 14% vs 18%); ADI beat, -13% pre-market. Low-bar misses get bought: BURL comps +1% 'disappointing', +8% pre-market.
- Anthropic (ANT): IPO $83 on 11-18/19, day-1 open 111.5 close 97.17 (vol 857M), 11-20 low 83.05, 11-23 close 87.64, 11-24 pre-market ~82.4-83 (below IPO price). NDX fast entry: announcement after close Dec 11, entry Dec 21 (funds buy at close Dec 18). Quiet-period expiry ~Dec 14 (underwriter initiations). SpaceX precedent (SPCX debut 6-12, joined NDX 7-7): no pre-inclusion run-up, -15% in 6 sessions after joining. Not a clean long or short; revisit if it closes <83 two days running.
- Retail prints 11-24: DKS EPS 1.94 vs 1.41 (Foot Locker comp +0.5%, DICK'S +2.6%, $903M buyback) +17% pre; DLTR comps +4.6% (traffic +3.8%), FY EPS raised to 8.05-8.25, tariff reinvestments cost $0.42/share; BBY comps +6.1% (best in 5 yrs, street 2.3%), FY EPS raised 6.90-7.05; ANF +11%; SHOE (Shoe Station, ex-Shoe Carnival) Q3 miss comps -5.1%, GM -570bp, -22% pre. Peers (DG +3.7, OLLI +2.1, FIVE +1.6, KSS +7.5) already moved at pre-market: sympathy is priced by the time I look. Upcoming: AEO, FIVE 12-02 AMC; M 12-02 BMO; DG ~early Dec; NKE ~Dec 18. IEEPA tariff refunds boost retailer EPS (DLTR Q2 had +$1.31) but DLTR is reinvesting in price.
- M&A: Sanofi buys Insmed $175/sh cash, $41B (11-24), close H1 2027; INSM ~170.7 pre-market (2.5% spread ~ cash-like), SNY +6.7%. No trade.
- Health insurers: CMS CRUSH proposed rule 11-16 (RADV back to PY2018, ~$9B/yr, comments to 1-19-2027). UNH fell 15% then stabilized; Jan-2026 analog did not bounce for months. Not traded.
- Trades so far: PUBM (11-06 long 4%, closed 11-13 +12.5%, +9.9 pts vs SPY). ROST (11-18 long 4% at 226.23, closed 11-20 around 208 pre-market, about -8%). No-trade sessions: 10-29, 11-04, 11-16, 11-17, 11-19, 11-20, 11-23, 11-24. Cash equity ~$100.5k.
- LESSONS:
 1) Peer-earnings-lag longs: PUBM worked (dated catalyst, peer lagged) but ROST failed (11-18 buy -> 11-20 print). Retail print reactions are driven by the NEXT quarter guide, not the FY raise. Avoid buying into a peer's print where the whisper needs a raise after a run-down in a falling tape.
 2) By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced (GDS -14.7% a day before I looked; cyber peers +4-6% pre-market on PANW; retail sympathy 11-24). The sympathy gap is in the fill price.
 3) Regulatory proposals (CRUSH) and big-cap drops can stay down for months: need a catalyst, not just a big drop (UNH Jan-2026 analog).
 4) In capitulation tapes (SPY 6 down days then +4.7% bounce), pre-open 'bounce' longs have a ~coin-flip edge. Cash is the position. Wait for stabilisation (VIX peak, index holding a gap-up) rather than catching.
 5) 11-24 process lesson: when binary information arrives BEFORE my next session's open (PCE 8:30 ET 11-25, DELL AMC 11-24), waiting a day is cheaper than holding through it. Shorts on 10%-daily-vol neoclouds (CRWV 40-70 range, NBIS) need >2:1 payoff; mid-range entries do not give it.
- Open ideas: HPE long after DELL reaction (8x guided EPS, 10% FCF yield, but margin-mix derating); neocloud shorts only after a squeeze to the upper range (CRWV 55+, NBIS 110) with stops above the 11-23 highs; ANT around Dec 11-18; NDX funds sell other mega-caps to fund ANT (mid-Dec); tower churn (AMT/CCI/SBAC); JBS/China beef quotas; MA-exposed clinic landlords; consumer-lending lead-gen (TREE) on more lender-pullback evidence; NKE into Dec 18 print after DKS/Foot Locker comp turn (weak); DG into early-Dec print.
